links.outcome: Privacy/plagiarism (memorization) of LLM-generated synthetic mental health reports
links.effect: All three models reportedly generated privacy-safe synthetic reports, with no compromise of patient confidentiality; no numeric results given in the abstract.
links.quote: The results demonstrate that all models can generate clinically coherent, diverse, and privacy-safe synthetic reports, significantly expanding the available training data for clinical natural language processing tasks without compromising patient confidentiality.

unlisted_practices: Multi-dimensional evaluation of LLM-generated synthetic clinical text for semantic fidelity, lexical diversity, and privacy/plagiarism
Using LLM-based synthetic data augmentation conditioned on ICD-10 codes to address data scarcity

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, OpenBioLLM, Qwen) for generating synthetic clinical mental health evaluation reports across fidelity, diversity, and privacy/memorization metrics without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard.
